grounding.states: 12 minutes for large eggs dropped into boiling water gives fully hard-boiled eggs
grounding.from: Healthline says 12 to 13 minutes gives fully hard-boiled eggs that are not over-cooked

grounding.states: 10 minutes for large eggs in boiling water gives a mostly cooked egg, slightly soft in the center
grounding.from: At 10 minutes, the eggs are mostly cooked through but slightly soft in the center.

grounding.states: past about 14 to 15 minutes, large eggs turn rubbery or dry
grounding.from: Past about 14–15 minutes the eggs turn rubbery or dry.

grounding.states: move the eggs to cold or ice water after cooking to stop the cooking
grounding.from: Several sources move the eggs to cold or ice water after cooking to stop the cooking.

value.answer: About 12 minutes for large eggs dropped into boiling water. That gets you a fully set yolk. At 10 minutes they're firm but a little soft in the middle, and past 14 or 15 they go rubbery and dry. Move them to cold water after so they stop cooking.
